messages:
mike: Heads-up — noticed a ~3x invoice delta for acct=globex after yesterday's rollout. Early signal looks correlated with requests that fell back to the quantized variant due to primary capacity. Anyone digging into billing events?

tina: Can you paste a sample invoice line or event? I want to see token counts and model tags.

mike: Sure — copied from invoice preview (redact ids):
```
invoice_line: tenant=globex tokens=48231 model_tag=redwood-7b-fp16 fallback_variant=redwood-7b-int8 quantity=48231 unit=token
invoice_line: tenant=globex tokens=48231 model_tag=redwood-7b-int8 fallback_variant=redwood-7b-int8 quantity=48231 unit=token
```
This is the suspicious part — same request appears twice with different model_tag fields (primary + fallback).

alexa: :eyes: Two quick hypotheses: (1) fallback path emits its own billing event without dedupe, (2) the quantized variant uses slightly different tokenization logic and both events count tokens independently.

jose: Logs I pulled show the router emitting a "request_forwarded" to both backends during a partial failure window. Looks like we don't suppress downstream billing event emission when the primary already accepted.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout redwood-7b-int8 -> 2026-03-17T21:12:00Z status=partial (20% routes)

sara: We should check the event-emitter service (metering-emitter) for dedupe keys. Right now we key on request_id + tenant, but router is sometimes fan-outing with different internal request_ids. We need a canonical request fingerprint that survives routing. Also add model_variant to schema so we can attribute but not double-charge. Metric to watch: metering.events_emitted and metering.duplicate_detected.

mike: Log extract from router + emitter showing fan-out and two event emissions: 
```
[2026-03-17T21:14:03Z] router: req_id=r-8a3 route=primary -> forwarded to 10.0.3.21
[2026-03-17T21:14:03Z] router: req_id=intern-xx route=fallback -> forwarded to 10.0.4.11
[2026-03-17T21:14:04Z] emitter: emitted billing_event id=e-987 request_fingerprint=fp-123 model=redwood-7b-fp16 tokens=48231
[2026-03-17T21:14:05Z] emitter: emitted billing_event id=e-988 request_fingerprint=fp-124 model=redwood-7b-int8 tokens=48231
```
Note fingerprint differs because the router generates new ids on fallback.

tina: Short-term mitigation: patch the emitter to consult a shared dedupe store (redis) using a stable tenant+user+client_req_id tuple and drop duplicates for N=30s. Low-risk and should stop double billing spikes. Also add an alert on billing.event_rate_increase for top-affected tenants.

billing-bot: Billing alert created: INC-1234 — flagged invoices for tenant globex; holding final invoice until reconciliation.

alexa: Long-term: we need to (A) stop router from fabricating new client-visible request ids on fallback — pass-through the original client_req_id, (B) canonicalize token counting in the serving runtime (single tokenizer library used for both fp16 and int8 code paths), and (C) include model_variant + route_tag in the event schema so attribution is explicit. Schema change will require careful rollout (consumer versions + schema migration).

sara: Agree. Also we should add a console panel: "fallback billing attribution" that breaks down per-tenant token deltas when fallback events occur. That will help CS and finance while we reconcile.

mike: Action items: 1) tina to open PR for emitter dedupe patch and hotfix deploy (ETA 2h), 2) infra to stop creating new request ids on fallback (short RFC), 3) sara/alexa to spec schema change + rollout plan (next-week), 4) product to add dashboard widget and a mailer for affected tenants. I'll assemble a short postmortem after we triage.

jose: I'll add router logs correlation keys to the observability trace so we can show the fan-out in the console.

mike: Thanks all — please ping here when PRs land. :thumbsup:
